ledger.claim: These three artifacts are one and the same trip, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied on the record before any argument about the route: the trip record, the driver's GPS trace and the fare ledger all carry trip_id TRP-00507, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-26T12:21:40 matches the trip record's started_at to the second. The rider's initial burden to show the artifacts describe the same journey is therefore discharged on the artifacts themselves.

The deviation is established, measured on the field that governs. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The trace measures 11.36 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 3.6 km: an excess of 7.76 km, 215.6% of optimal. Both establishment limbs pass — 7.76 km is greater than 0.8 km absolute and greater than 20% of 3.6 km — so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

The excess is not merely established, it is MATERIAL: 215.6% of optimal is more than four times the 50% materiality figure in POL-RD-01. Materiality is what engages the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06, and it is also why this is not a lane-change or a forced U-turn — the rider was carried 7.76 km further than the route the platform quoted for the journey.

The trace that carries this finding is clean, so the finding may rest on it alone. The artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issues: 127 fixes at a 10 second sample interval against an expected 10 second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of the three impairment limbs in POL-RD-07 fires — there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds — so the POL-RD-07 consequences and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged and no independent corroboration is required.

The driver's own trace shows 21 minutes of driving between its first and last fix (12:21:40 to 12:42:40) against a booked optimal of 7 minutes at speeds reaching 34 kph — consistent with a long diversion rather than the 3.6 km hop the platform quoted. The trip record's own derived deviation status, computed from this trace in code, is 'material'.

The refund regime is the metered one. The fare_breakdown carries fare_model METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the money and POL-RD-11 is unavailable: there is no quoted_fare_sgd on this trip, and the premise of POL-RD-11 — a rider already whole on distance and time because the price was fixed at booking — simply does not exist here. The rider paid the meter for the detour and the meter must be recomputed.

The vehicle type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not re-base the threshold to any matched itinerary and no co-rider collection distance is in issue. The baseline is the booked optimal of 3.6 km on the trip record, and nothing in the record displaces it.

No relocation clause can rescue this route. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null, so there was no amended endpoint for POL-RD-05 to re-quote against and the booked optimal stands. The driver's 'Changi Beach is very long, she couldn't tell me which car park' is an account of a choice he made, not a recorded amendment of the destination.

There is no rider instruction anywhere in the record, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run in the driver's favour. The chat export for this trip holds zero messages — message_count 0, messages [] — and the trip record agrees at chat_message_count 0. POL-RD-04 requires a rider message timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor, and the corroborating waypoint field it insists on (chat_message.waypoint_hint) does not exist because there is no message to carry one. The driver's suggestion that he was asked and could not be told which car park has no artifact behind it.

The driver offers no external traffic cause that could exonerate any part of the excess, and the advisory artifact is MISSING. I disclose the impairment expressly: EV-ADVIS-00507-01 has admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and no advisory covers Airport Boulevard or Changi Coast Rd in this window. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be satisfied — there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, no validity window and no corridor departure-and-rejoin to match — and under POL-RD-13 the driver's bare account of choosing a route carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because no party cites an advisory identifier, the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and it is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation.

The refund is arithmetic and it is 9.80. Running POL-RD-02 on the metered fare: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 3.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 7.0 optimal min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 6.00 fixed surcharge properly chargeable because this trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 3 + ERP of 0.00 + waiting_time_fee of 0.00 - promo_discount of 0.00 = 15.26. Refund = charged_total 25.03 - 15.26 = 9.77 before rounding, and 9.77 rounds UP to 9.80. The fare_breakdown's own derived block publishes the same figures, so the arithmetic can be re-checked by hand.

The outcome on the money is PARTIAL_REFUND and it must not be rounded down to nothing or up to everything. The refund of 9.77 exceeds the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor in POL-RD-02, so no de minimis NO_ACTION applies; it is 39.0% of charged_total, far below the 90% threshold at which POL-RD-02 would require FULL_REFUND. Under POL-GEN-03 that is a partial refund to the filing party, and it changes the present state: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the rider is presently carrying the whole 25.03 including the 9.77 attributable to a route he never asked for.

No pass-through correction is added on top, and I say so plainly rather than inflating the claim: POL-RD-09(1) forbids double-counting, and here there is nothing to double-count because erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00 — the trip crossed no gantry and the optimal-route ERP is 0.00 against an off-optimal-route ERP total of 0.00. The 6.00 airport surcharge is not a billing-integrity defect either: it is properly chargeable on a trip originating at the airport and it is already inside the recomputed fare under POL-RD-02, not an add-on.

This case is decidable and should be decided, not escalated. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across all three core artifacts, the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no timestamps contradict, the refund of 9.77 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, and every charge line has a counterpart — the surcharge is matched by an airport-origin trip and the distance and time lines are matched by the driver's own trace. Escalation here would hold the disputed amount on evidence that is complete and unanimous, and the rider would be left carrying the charge POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 say he should not.

I do not press the POL-RD-06 uplift, and I say why rather than stretch the record: the pattern test is not met. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 250 completed trips in the last 90 days — a ratio of 0, well under the 0.05 figure the clause requires — so no repeat pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total is licensed and no driver-conduct referral arises on these figures. The deviation finding rests on this trip's trace alone, exactly as POL-GEN-01 requires, and the driver's profile is not used to establish anything about this trip.

The ledger records tolls_erp 0.00, optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00, no erp_gantries, and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding off-route ERP on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, because that figure is already charged_total less a recomputed fare that includes only on-optimal-route charges. ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this trip is decided on the driver's own GPS trace, and the money outcome is a partial refund of SGD 9.80 to the rider.

THE ROUTE. The trace (EV-GPS-00507) measures 11.36 km between the recorded pickup at Changi Airport Terminal 3 and the recorded dropoff at Nicoll Drive, against a booked optimal route of 3.6 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00507). That is 7.76 km of excess, 215.6% of optimal. Both establishment tests in POL-RD-01 pass (more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED; and because the excess exceeds 50% it is additionally MATERIAL. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the trace figure of 11.36 km; the trip record's rounded 11.4 km and its 216.7% convenience figure were not used for the threshold test, as the clause requires.

NOTHING EXCUSES THE EXCESS. The chat export for this trip is empty (EV-CHAT-00507: message_count 0, messages [], and the trip record agrees at chat_message_count 0), so no rider instruction is recorded and POL-RD-04 cannot be run in the driver's favour; for the same reason its waypoint corroboration test could not be run at all. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amended endpoint to re-quote against; the driver's explanation that Changi Beach is long and he chose a quiet spot describes a choice he made, not a recorded change of destination. No traffic advisory exists for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00507-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and it is named here because the ruling touches it. Its absence decides nothing — nothing rests on it — and POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable, since no advisory names a road the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window or is matched by a corridor departure and rejoin. No party cites an advisory identifier, so under POL-RD-13 the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle and not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact; POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure.

THE MONEY (POL-RD-02 on a metered fare). Charged_total: SGD 25.03. Recomputed_fare: SGD 15.26 = base fare 3.80 + distance 0.75 x 3.6 optimal km = 2.70 + time 0.28 x 7.0 optimal min = 1.96, all at the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00507), + platform fee 0.80 + airport surcharge 6.00 + ERP 0.00 + waiting time 0.00 - promo 0.00. Refund: 25.03 - 15.26 = SGD 9.77 before rounding, rounded UP to SGD 9.80, the amount this ruling moves.

The 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable and stays inside the recomputed fare: the trip originated at Changi Airport on Wednesday 26 August 2026 at 12:15, outside the Friday/Saturday/Sunday 17:00-23:59 peak window, so the off-peak figure applies. It is not a phantom line, and no billing-integrity referral arises. No pass-through correction is added on top: the ledger shows no ERP gantries and no tolls, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding off-route ERP to the POL-RD-02 figure in any event.

WHY PARTIAL AND NOT FULL OR NONE. The refund of 9.77 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so no de minimis no-action applies. It is 39.0% of the charged total, far below the 90% at which POL-RD-02 requires a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund and not a full one. POL-RD-11 does not apply — the fare model is METERED and there is no quoted fare — and POL-RD-12 does not re-base the threshold because the vehicle type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL. No unbilled-distance shortfall arises either: the meter charged 11.4 km against the trace's 11.36 km, so no driver compensation is owed.

THE PROFILE CHECK. Because the deviation is material, POL-RD-06 was consulted. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250 — a ratio of 0.00 — so neither gate is met, no repeat pattern is established, no full-refund uplift is licensed and no driver-conduct referral arises. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags figure is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used to establish anything about this trip.

NO ESCALATION. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare ledger; the trace is unimpaired (127 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) do not fire and no independent corroboration is required); no timestamps contradict; the refund is far below both ceilings; and every charge line has a counterpart in the record. The rider's account of the conversation and the driver's account of it are noted, but the conversation itself is evidenced nowhere, so nothing turns on what was said; the driver's statement carries no weight multiplier and so does not affect the confidence figure. Confidence rests on the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts, and is 0.93.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
